messages.content: Get the latest closing prices and volumes for Apple Inc., Google LLC., and Microsoft Corporation in the New York Stock Exchange

function.name: get_stock_data
function.description: Retrieve the most recent trading day's closing price and volume for a specified stock. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

symbol.description: The stock symbol of the company.

data_points.description: The type of data you want to retrieve for the stock. This can include closing price, opening price, volume, etc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the latest closing prices and volumes for Apple Inc., Google LLC., and Microsoft Corporation in the NYSE. Actually Apple (AAPL) is on NASDAQ, not NYSE. Google (Alphabet) is also on NASDAQ. Microsoft (MSFT) is on NASDAQ. But the user says "in the New York Stock Exchange". That might be a mistake; maybe they just want the latest closing prices and volumes for those companies. We need to use the function get_stock_data. The function signature: get_stock_data(symbol: string, data_points: "price" | "volume"[]). Wait data_points is either "price" or "volume" array? It says data_points: "price" | "volume"[]. That seems odd: it expects either "price" or an array of "volume"? Probably it's a mistake. Maybe we should call get_stock_data with symbol and data_points as ["price", "volume"]. But the type says data_points: "price" | "volume"[], so we could pass "price" or an array of "volume"? That doesn't make sense. I think we should pass data_points: ["price", "volume"].

We need to call the function for each symbol: AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT. Or we can combine them? The function only accepts one symbol at a time. So we need to call three times. But the user asked for all three. We can do separate calls. Let's do that. We'll call get_stock_data for each symbol with data_points: ["price", "volume"]. Then we will return the results.
